title: Flatness in the quotient relation
as_he_states: Can flatness replace the smoothness used in the quotient-relation argument on the reused GIT leaf?
plausible_today: A represented flat locally finitely presented equivalence relation admits an algebraic-space sheaf quotient under the usual hypotheses; descent to a scheme and finite type require additional assumptions.
state_of_art: Mumford–Fogarty §0 fixes the geometric-quotient conventions; Hashimoto proves finite-type results for universal strict orbit spaces. Neither is a literal answer to the incomplete margin.
why_open: The retained margin omits the surrounding hypotheses; no source states why the author left it.
worth: Worth a short source-and-ink check, because one missing qualifier changes the category of quotient.

title: Finite type of an orbit quotient
as_he_states: The typed source expects the algebraicity assumption on the quotient to be unnecessary.
plausible_today: For a flat finite-type group scheme over a noetherian base, a universal strict orbit space has the finite-type property asserted in Hashimoto’s theorem.
state_of_art: The checked GIT second-edition footnote says the question was settled by Fogarty; Hashimoto gives a primary modern proof in an explicitly stated quotient setting.
why_open: The original retained typed version predates the checked revised footnote; no date of reuse or authorial priority is inferred.
worth: A bibliographic task of modest interest; the relevant theorem is established.

title: A doubled Picard extension
as_he_states: Construct the displayed lift and split the Picard/NS extension after pullback by2.
plausible_today: A homomorphic lift s with hs=2id splits the pullback extension; a canonical sheaf-level construction needs the base and rigidifications specified.
state_of_art: The cube identity and symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition are checked in Moonen et al. II2.12; the exact unfinished lift is not identified.
why_open: The page ends mid-construction. No reason beyond the interruption is supplied.
worth: Worth a few hours to identify the precise Picard functor and its2-torsion obstruction.

title: All amended finite invariant-cycle cases
as_he_states: Extend the degree-one invariant-cycle exact sequence to the inserted arbitrary-n cases, with the Brauer term θ(n).
plausible_today: Prime-to-p étale Kummer gives the displayed mechanism; p-primary statements need flat cohomology, a specified Picard functor and the exact geometric assumptions.
state_of_art: Raynaud1970 §§6,8 and SGA7 IX12.1 identify divisor and curve ingredients. The complete amended sequence with all alternatives has not been located exactly.
why_open: The page changes the prime restrictions and adds the obstruction; it does not explain a later abandonment.
worth: High-interest identification task: trace the1967 announcements against the1970 full paper before proposing a new theorem.

title: Factorization of total multiplicity gcd
as_he_states: The inserted expression identifies gcd(μ_i d_i) with gcd(d_i)gcd(μ_i).
plausible_today: The total multiplicity/index formula is valid in Raynaud’s curve setting; the separate gcd factorization requires a further relation on the geometric data.
state_of_art: The unrestricted arithmetic identity is disproved by (d_i)=(2,3),(μ_i)=(1,2). Raynaud §7.1 and SGA7 IX12.1 are the exact geometric comparison targets.
why_open: No justification is written for this inserted simplification.
worth: Worth an ink check and then a geometric realizability test; the numerical example alone does not refute a geometric theorem.

title: Which vertical torsion is the NS kernel?
as_he_states: Is R=ker(Γ→NS(X_s)) the full torsion subgroup of Γ?
plausible_today: R⊂tors Γ is cyclic; equality holds in the appropriate relative-curve comparison. In higher dimension P^0 and P^τ must be distinguished.
state_of_art: Raynaud Theorem6.4.1 proves E∩P^τ=tors E. Proposition8.1.2 specializes to curves. It does not replace P^τ by P^0 in arbitrary dimension.
why_open: The page explicitly asks the kernel question after using only a finite cyclic subgroup.
worth: High interest: isolate the quotient P^τ/P^0 and its interaction with vertical divisors in a concrete higher-dimensional model.

title: Brauer transition maps in the inverse limit
as_he_states: Pass from bounded-exponent obstruction groups to their zero inverse limit.
plausible_today: The conclusion follows for the actual multiplication-by-l Kummer transitions and uniformly bounded l-exponent; it is false for arbitrary transition maps.
state_of_art: The Kummer diagram and the direct argument x_i=l^N x_(i+N) settle the step; Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov §1.4 and§4.3 supply the surrounding Brauer facts.
why_open: The manuscript omits the transition-map computation, not necessarily the needed structure.
worth: Low remaining research interest after the check; retain it as a proof obligation for the companion edition.

title: Cancelled injectivity proofs and Raynaud’s exact locator
as_he_states: Obtain the needed injectivity through the cited Raynaud theorem after the preliminary proofs are cancelled.
plausible_today: Use Raynaud’s separated Picard/divisor theory under its actual hypotheses; do not revive the cancelled cover argument.
state_of_art: Raynaud1970 §6.4 is relevant, but the cited short-announcement th.3/prop.7(ii) numbering remains unresolved.
why_open: The cancellations and appeal to Raynaud are explicit; no external reason for abandoning the sketches is known.
worth: Worth a targeted bibliographic session because an exact locator would settle several dependent statuses.

title: Weakening regularity to local factoriality
as_he_states: The margin suggests weakening the regularity hypothesis to local factoriality in the divisor argument.
plausible_today: The Cartier-divisor lattice step only needs local factoriality; other uses of resolution, smoothness and Picard representability must be checked separately.
state_of_art: Raynaud §§6.1.11,8.1.4 use local factoriality in precise results. They do not establish an unrestricted replacement throughout the full manuscript proof.
why_open: The margin marks a local weakening, not a revised complete theorem.
worth: Worth separating the proof dependencies; a few hours should settle the lattice part, not the entire p-primary statement.

title: Arithmetic orthogonality beyond a trait
as_he_states: Prove orthogonality over the broader written adic base using Frobenius weights and torsion finiteness.
plausible_today: The arithmetic argument gives the specified pairing vanishing/inclusion. Equality of the orthogonal complement requires rank or geometric input.
state_of_art: SGA7 IX2.6(a) explicitly separates this arithmetic inclusion from Theorem2.4 over a henselian trait.
why_open: The manuscript changes ambient bases and leaves the equality mechanism unstated; no source claims the broader formulation solved.
worth: High interest only after the base and finiteness assumptions are fixed; otherwise it is an underdetermined extension.

title: Finite subgroup closure and specialization
as_he_states: Control finite closures of generic torsion and their special-fibre pairings over the written base.
plausible_today: Finite étale lifting is controlled over proper henselian bases; arbitrary finite flat torsion and general adic bases require separate representability and flatness hypotheses.
state_of_art: Stacks0A48 and09ZL give exact finite-étale equivalences. They do not assert smoothness of a finite flat p-group scheme.
why_open: The leaf queries or uses the relevant closure property without a full uniform construction.
worth: Worth a focused comparison with the precise model category, not a blanket finite-group-scheme assertion.

title: One model for every torsion level
as_he_states: Choose a finite-type model or extension that works simultaneously for all ν.
plausible_today: Finite-level descent gives ∀ν∃K′; uniformity requires a single finite amount of geometric data or a separate l-adic finiteness theorem.
state_of_art: SGA7 IX2.6(a) makes the arithmetic reduction in its stated setting. No source exactly matches the manuscript’s broader adic-base all-level assertion.
why_open: The question mark is explicitly attached to the all-level model step.
worth: High-interest short task: identify the finite presentation data controlling the whole Tate tower.

title: Equivalence of polarization corollaries
as_he_states: The equivalence of two corollaries is left to the reader.
plausible_today: The stated polarization-induced isogeny compares the rational pairings; clearing its denominator and using torsion-free Tate lattices gives the integral vanishing implication.
state_of_art: SGA7 IX2.5 provides the published polarization comparison; the linear-algebra step is supplied in the proof audit.
why_open: It is left as an exercise, not presented as an open conjecture.
worth: No new research needed; include the short proof in the companion commentary.

title: Geometric meaning of the discriminant form
as_he_states: Identify the explicit lattice pairing with the obstruction from the Poincaré biextension, and understand weighted perfectness.
plausible_today: Under the regular relative-curve hypotheses and a rational point, compare with the restricted intersection pairing; retain residue-field and weight qualifications.
state_of_art: SGA7 VIII7.1(b) supplies the extension obstruction. Bosch–Lorenzini Theorem4.6 identifies the Jacobian pairing and Corollary4.7 specifies its perfectness cases.
why_open: The manuscript asserts geometric meaning after an abstract calculation; it does not include the full comparison proof.
worth: High interest for a concrete weighted example, with a few-hour run capable of computing the two finite groups and their comparison map.

title: Henselianity versus formal inverse closure
as_he_states: Does henselianity of the A_n imply closure under all formal inverse maps, and what is the smallest such family?
plausible_today: Implicit algebraic equations are controlled by henselian-pair criteria; arbitrary chosen formal-coordinate inverses are a separate closure property unless the family is explicitly the algebraic power-series system.
state_of_art: Stacks09XD/09XI give the exact henselian definition. Modern Weierstrass systems add closure axioms stronger than the manuscript’s bare question.
why_open: The first draft asks the converse and proposes algebraic series as a test case without a proof.
worth: High interest: compare minimal H-closure with henselization in a fixed coefficient field.

title: Smallest flow-closed family
as_he_states: Require closure under formal flows, including time-dependent fields, and obtain primitives and elementary transcendental functions.
plausible_today: The extra flow axiom gives these solutions; henselian/algebraic-series closure alone does not, since exp(t) is not algebraic in characteristic0.
state_of_art: Formal ODE recursion and the autonomous-time construction are checked; modern analytic systems and formal Frobenius provide comparisons, not an exact classification of the minimal A-family.
why_open: The pages introduce desired closure properties rather than prove their minimal realization.
worth: Worth a few-hour axiomatic closure construction; a full classification is a larger project.

title: BCH integration inside A
as_he_states: The Hausdorff formal-group construction should work in the chosen family; the sketch ends after reduction using Ado.
plausible_today: Formal BCH exists over characteristic-zero fields. Membership in A needs a proof from the actual flow and substitution axioms, with no illicit formal evaluation at1.
state_of_art: The ambient formal Frobenius theorem is checked; the exact A-membership theorem has not been identified in the searched analytic/formal literature.
why_open: The argument stops at its stated reduction; no later source explaining the omission was found.
worth: High-interest proof-completion task, starting with a nilpotent matrix Lie algebra and then auditing the Ado step.

title: Pfaff converse in a restricted function class
as_he_states: Integrate a regular involutive Pfaff system in A; compare the rank-one case with flow closure.
plausible_today: The ambient formal Frobenius theorem holds over characteristic-zero fields; A-valued first integrals require an additional closure theorem or axiom.
state_of_art: Bolsinov–Zuev Theorem2 proves the ambient theorem. The wholly cancelled39:8 retraction draft is not a second proof.
why_open: The converse is expressly desired, and the following attempted geometric formulation is cancelled.
worth: High interest, but begin with rank2 and a precisely generated family; the full arbitrary-A question exceeds a short session.

title: Projective and finite module coordinates
as_he_states: Replace free finite coordinate modules by projective modules, perhaps all finite modules.
plausible_today: Finite projective modules permit coordinate-free smooth formal affine spaces and local descent. Arbitrary finite modules can define singular spaces and need a broader category.
state_of_art: Strickland formal schemes provide the ambient setting; no exact treatment of this A-family extension was identified.
why_open: The page explicitly asks both extensions, with no claimed construction.
worth: Moderate interest: the finite-projective descent problem is feasible; keep arbitrary finite modules separate.

title: Transverse products before H
as_he_states: Construct transverse fibre products in the A-category under the axioms then in force.
plausible_today: H supplies the needed inverse-coordinate construction. Under the earlier axioms alone, closure of the solution in A has not been established.
state_of_art: Chiu–Hauser Lemma1.2 proves the ambient inverse theorem, not selected-family closure.
why_open: The assertion precedes the added inverse-closure axiom.
worth: Worth a short dependency audit and an explicit two-equation example.

title: Rejected evaluation at1 and its repair
as_he_states: Use an inverse formal map to prove ambient-unit closure; the text rejects its own evaluation at1.
plausible_today: H gives the Jacobson property of the augmentation ideal. H+D gives full ambient-unit reflection by extracting the coefficient of the auxiliary variable.
state_of_art: The proof audit supplies both repairs and the full H-only counterfamily Z+(t)Q[[t]]. Henselian-pair references verify the target notion.
why_open: The text itself identifies the illegal evaluation and continues with a weaker statement.
worth: No new theorem is needed for these two conclusions; the scan should decide which stronger assertion survives.

title: Henselian factor lifting from H
as_he_states: Deduce coprime-factor lifting and the implicit-function theorem from inverse closure.
plausible_today: The coefficient multiplication map has unit Sylvester determinant; H and zero evaluation give the lift, together with the Jacobson property.
state_of_art: The direct proof is supplied; Stacks09XD/09XI give equivalent henselian criteria and Chiu–Hauser gives the ambient inverse criterion.
why_open: The pages sketch rather than fully expand the determinant and the permitted substitution.
worth: Low remaining research interest; useful as a complete companion proof.

title: Faithful flatness of the ambient formal ring
as_he_states: Is k[[t_1,…,t_n]] faithfully flat over A_n if k is faithfully flat over A_0?
plausible_today: Under a D-only reading the polynomial family is a counterexample to faithfulness. Under H+D the question needs a new argument or a full-family counterexample.
state_of_art: Modern Weierstrass/analytic systems have extra hypotheses; none of the opened results certifies arbitrary A-families. The polynomial counterexample is carefully restricted to its admissible reading.
why_open: A margin asks the question, and the letter d has changed meaning between drafts.
worth: Very high interest once the ink fixes d; a few-hour run can test coherent/noetherian examples, not settle all families.

title: Ordinary versus divided derivatives
as_he_states: The characteristic-zero margin suggests ordinary derivative closure is equivalent to divided derivative closure.
plausible_today: This holds for a Q-algebra coefficient ring. Characteristic0 alone does not permit division by factorials.
state_of_art: Hasse identities are recomputed. Z[t,t²/2] disproves the bare ring inference, but is not offered as a complete H/composition family.
why_open: The manuscript shifts from a field draft to an arbitrary-ring draft.
worth: Worth fixing the precise coefficient assumption; a full-family counterexample would be a separate task.

title: Functorial principal parts and differential operators
as_he_states: Give infinitesimal neighborhoods and differential operators canonical A-structures, compatible with transverse pullback.
plausible_today: In A-charts, Hasse identities and coefficient extraction verify the construction. Globalization needs coordinate-change/descent hypotheses.
state_of_art: The local calculation is checked; the exact arbitrary-A globalization is not identified in Strickland or the analytic-structure literature.
why_open: The leaf lists functorial properties without a complete descent proof.
worth: Moderate interest: formulate and prove the chart-transition lemma first.

title: Induced structures and smooth completion sections
as_he_states: Construct the induced A-structure on a smooth formal subspace and a section in the smooth-completion situation.
plausible_today: With an A-transverse chart, the graph criterion gives uniqueness and local existence; an unnamed global construction cannot be supplied from the leaf alone.
state_of_art: The ambient inverse theorem and formal smooth geometry are established comparisons. No exact unrestricted A-section theorem was located.
why_open: The construction is unnamed and relies on earlier desired closure properties.
worth: Worth a short proof audit in affine charts before attempting projective descent.

title: Integral quotient effectivity
as_he_states: Make the relation defined by an integrable distribution effective in the A-category; decipher the X/X′ target in the quotient criterion.
plausible_today: A regular formal distribution has a local ambient quotient in characteristic0. Effectivity and A-membership are additional requirements.
state_of_art: Bolsinov–Zuev Theorem2 settles the ambient first-integral statement, not arbitrary A-effectivity.
why_open: The leaf introduces this as a further axiom rather than deriving it.
worth: High interest if pursued after the Pfaff problem; first specify the relation and its categorical quotient.

title: Division with a complete linear topology
as_he_states: Prove unique division and regularity for a distinguished series over a separated complete linearly topological ring.
plausible_today: The full statement holds with finitely many topologically nilpotent lower coefficients and a unit leading coefficient.
state_of_art: Strickland FPFP Theorem33.1/Corollary33.2 match the scope. The proof audit supplies the discrete-quotient and nilpotent-filtration argument, retaining the full unit series.
why_open: The manuscript abandons two proof routes, then supplies a third. Its final scalar notation is a reading alarm, not cancellation of the theorem.
worth: No open theorem remains here; a few-hour task could produce a clean constructive companion with explicit precision control.

title: An adic local-to-global spectral sequence
as_he_states: Can the finite-coefficient nearby-cycle spectral sequence pass to the proposed ℓ-adic limit with constructibility and suitable projective systems?
plausible_today: Use compatible constructible adic complexes and derived inverse limits; finite global groups alone do not justify an ordinary inverse limit of sheaves.
state_of_art: Deligne SGA4½, Finitude3.2, and the later adic nearby-cycle formalism supply constructibility. This resolves the missing finiteness input, with a modern categorical formulation.
why_open: The author explicitly reserves limit verifications and adds the constructibility/system requirement.
worth: A precise comparison of the manuscript inverse-system conventions with the derived formulation is useful; a new finiteness theorem is not suggested.

title: The smooth-case transition multiplier
as_he_states: Reduce to X=S and verify the support-cohomology transition written as multiplication by the finite field-extension degree.
plausible_today: The divisor class pulls back by the ramification index e. Field degree is equal to e only after suitable residue/defect hypotheses; a tame ℓ-power tower still kills the colimit.
state_of_art: Absolute purity and Gysin functoriality establish the corrected multiplier. The explicit imperfect-residue extension in proof_audit.md §11 has [L:K]=p and e=1.
why_open: The verification is explicitly left to the reduction X=S. No reason beyond that omission is documented.
worth: High-value short correction: retain the smooth-acyclicity proof but replace its multiplier and state the killing tower.

title: What is the Griffiths result referred to here?
as_he_states: A normal-crossing monodromy discussion refers to a result of Griffiths without a complete citation.
plausible_today: Identify the exact text and the particular bound, filtration or complex-geometric hypothesis intended before assigning a publication match.
state_of_art: The general i+1 monodromy bound is independently verified in Illusie2021 Theorem2.3. The precise Griffiths bibliographic identity remains unresolved: class F, not an unproved mathematical conjecture.
why_open: The supplied passage gives no complete bibliographic locator.
worth: Worth an archive/ink and correspondence lookup; thematic Griffiths citations are not an adequate identification.

title: Absolute purity for regular schemes
as_he_states: Every regular scheme should satisfy the stated cohomological purity theorem; mixed characteristic is historically singled out as unproved.
plausible_today: For a regular closed immersion of codimension c between noetherian regular schemes, with n invertible, Ri!Λ≃Λ(−c)[−2c].
state_of_art: Gabber absolute purity, as proved in Riou2014 ExposéXVI Theorem3.1.1, settles this formulation without an excellence assumption. The coefficient invertibility remains necessary.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly states the historical conjecture and available restrictions; its written context is not a present-day claim.
worth: Settled. Useful as an exact source-concordance task and for checking every subsequent twist and shift.

title: The second square in the residue diagram
as_he_states: The two localization sequences and cup products should form a morphism of exact sequences; the second square is admitted pending verification.
plausible_today: Choose the Kummer boundary and Gysin conventions together. The boundary is a graded derivation; the sign depends on whether the Kummer class is the left or right cup factor.
state_of_art: Riou2014 §§2--4 gives Gysin and Kummer compatibility, including an explicitly opposite root-torsor sign in Lemma3.4.8. proof_audit.md §12 provides the derived localization verification in a fixed convention.
why_open: The author explicitly says the second square seems to need checking.
worth: Worth a small fully signed lemma, especially before implementing the exterior-power formula; no unresolved purity theorem remains here.

title: The coefficient scope of principal-divisor restriction
as_he_states: Restriction from the partially punctured strict-local scheme to the last divisor is asserted to be an isomorphism in the displayed induction.
plausible_today: The sufficient inherited hypothesis is that the locally constant coefficient extends to the original strict-local X. Arbitrary locally constant coefficients on U′ need not satisfy the restriction assertion.
state_of_art: The Artin–Schreier example in proof_audit.md §12 disproves the broad interpretation. The inherited coefficient scope is a reading problem; the repaired assertion for coefficients extending to X is verified. It is not an unresolved modern theorem.
why_open: No explicit authorial doubt is attached to the scope; this is a mathematically motivated reading problem, not an attributed open question.
worth: High value: inspect the carried F-convention before treating the induction as a general theorem with arbitrary local coefficients.

title: Resolution and the full nearby-cycle programme
as_he_states: It seems plausible that resolution-based nearby-cycle results extend to excellent traits in all characteristics, and to arbitrary U with the full rather than tame sheaves.
plausible_today: Separate the geometric resolution conjecture from constructibility and quasi-unipotence of nearby cycles. The latter have proofs that do not settle the former.
state_of_art: Deligne Finitude3.2 supplies constructibility and Illusie2021 Theorem2.3 gives monodromy. Temkin2024 still formulates the relevant general local-uniformization/resolution problems; no proof of arbitrary resolution was identified.
why_open: The manuscript expressly calls both extensions plausible. No authorial reason for abandoning them is inferred.
worth: Do not pursue broad resolution as a short project. A worthwhile finite task is to inventory which exact consequences survive without it.

title: Wild inertia on a normal-crossing degeneration
as_he_states: Does wild inertia P act trivially on the full nearby-cycle sheaves, and on proper generic cohomology, under the written normal-crossing and prime-to-p multiplicity assumptions?
plausible_today: Under the corresponding log-smooth normal-crossing hypotheses, compare full and tame nearby cycles; for proper log-smooth families also allow the stated open-stratum version.
state_of_art: Rapoport--Zink1982 §2 and Nakayama1998 Theorem0.1/Corollary0.1.1 settle the tame behaviour. Illusie2002 Theorem8.3 and Corollaries8.4,8.4.3 give the precise log-smooth comparison, including nonvertical situations.
why_open: The author explicitly asks the local question and says the global cohomological statement is not then proved.
worth: Settled in the verified hypotheses. Preserve the distinction between trivial wild action and nontrivial tame unipotence.

title: The integral monodromy filtration qualifier
as_he_states: The normal-crossing calculation should give a canonical finite filtration with inertia-trivial graded pieces; the transcription includes a stronger integral purity qualifier.
plausible_today: The rational/integral filtration from the relevant spectral sequence is defined, but saturation of every lattice step requires a distinct argument and may depend on torsion.
state_of_art: The i+1 nilpotence bound is verified. No exact source for the additional saturated/pure integral formulation on this leaf was identified; class C is limited to that qualifier.
why_open: This is a distinct reading-and-hypothesis issue; the author does not flag the whole nilpotence theorem as open.
worth: Worth a focused torsion example and source check, after fixing which integral filtration is intended.

title: A general Kummer tower need not reduce dimension by one
as_he_states: For strict-local noetherian X of dimension n and U=D(t), is cdℓ U(∞)≤n−1 after adjoining all prime-to-p roots of t?
plausible_today: The assertion is false in the stated arbitrary noetherian generality. More restrictive excellent or geometrically normal-crossing settings must be treated separately.
state_of_art: Orgogozo2014 XVIII_B §§2.1--2.4 constructs a dimension-two regular strict-local nonexcellent A with H³(D(t),Z/ℓ)≠0. Since the tower group has cdℓ=1, Cartan--Leray implies cdℓ U(∞)≥2. This last deduction is ours, not a literal statement of Orgogozo.
why_open: The manuscript asks the question explicitly and notes that its cited standard conjecture would yield only n.
worth: High-value resolved obstruction. The follow-up is to isolate the best valid additional hypotheses, without calling every narrower variant open.

title: Lefschetz consequences and the lci improvement
as_he_states: The global and local Lefschetz bounds are conditional on purity, resolution and affine Lefschetz; a sharper i≤n−d vanishing for lci fibres is deferred.
plausible_today: Use rectified depth, Gabber affine Lefschetz and perverse nearby cycles. If X/S is flat lci of relative dimension n, usual RΦΛ[n] is perverse; support dimension d gives the stated shifted lower bound.
state_of_art: SGA7 I4.5--4.7 proves the historical characteristic-zero local results. Illusie2003 §§2.6,2.7,2.10 extends the depth/lci statements over general traits. Pilloni--Stroh2014 Theorem1.1.2 supplies affine Lefschetz.
why_open: The author lists the missing ingredients and expressly defers the sharper assertion.
worth: Settled after precise lci and coefficient hypotheses. A useful task is a single table translating rectified depth and the manuscript shift.

title: Checking the pinching counterexample
as_he_states: Pinch two sections together only over the closed point to obtain the example showing the need for the stronger hypotheses.
plausible_today: Two proper connected generic components specialize to a connected special fibre. The map on H0 is diagonal and Φman¹≠0. The special fibre has embedded nilpotent structure at the pinch.
state_of_art: The affine fibre-product construction and H0 calculation are independently checked in proof_audit.md §18; no conclusion that this is a flat lci family is drawn.
why_open: The manuscript sketches the example, with a doubtful H exponent; it is not a conjecture.
worth: A useful small example to retain, because suppressing the embedded structure would produce a false lci counterexample.

title: Uniformity in the punctured-fibre vanishing premise
as_he_states: A vanishing statement at x is used to deduce vanishing of hypercohomology on the punctured special fibre and the local comparison.
plausible_today: Require the relevant Φman sheaves to vanish throughout the punctured special fibre, equivalently at all its geometric points. An isolated nonsmooth point gives this sufficient condition.
state_of_art: Original SGA7 I4.5 proof(1) explicitly ranges over generizations of x. The corrected inference and degree boundaries are independently proved in proof_audit.md §19.
why_open: This is a substantive mathematical omission in the supplied wording; it is not presented as an authorial open problem.
worth: High-value local repair. The omitted point and the punctured support must not be interchanged.
